import pixeltable as pxt

# Initialize Pixeltable client
pxt.create_client()

# Get reference to the existing videos table
videos = pxt.get_table('videos')

# Create a view that expands each video into frame-level rows
# sampled at 1 fps using the built-in frame extraction iterator
frames_view = pxt.create_view(
    'video_frames',
    select=videos.select(
        # Include all original columns from videos table
        videos,
        # Extract frames at 1 fps using the built-in iterator
        pxt.io.FrameIterator(
            videos.video,
            fps=1
        ).as_('frame')
    )
)

print(f"Frame-level view created: {frames_view.name}")
print(f"Total rows: {frames_view.count()}")

import pixeltable as pxt

pxt.create_client()

videos = pxt.get_table('videos')

# Create a view that expands each video into frame-level rows

        # Include all original columns from videos table
        videos,
        # Extract frames at 1 fps using the built-in iterator

            videos.video,
            fps=1
        ).as_('frame')
